question: Why did the integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still show a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits?
expect: premise false: after system expansion the net climate-change impact was negative, −2,257.14 kg CO2-eq per t (a net benefit) (abstract)

<document title="Environmental and Preliminary Economic Assessment of Integrated Resource Recovery from Spent Fluid Catalytic Cracking Catalysts">

The integrated spent FCC catalyst recovery route still showed a net climate-change burden after product-substitution credits because the credits were scenario-dependent and did not eliminate the foreground emissions. The foreground system includes catalyst pretreatment, alkaline roasting, wet grinding/leaching, adsorption/desorption, product recovery, hazardous-component immobilization of the leaching residue, porous-substrate preparation, and composite phase-change-material preparation. The foreground emissions were not fully offset by the product-substitution credits, resulting in a net climate-change burden.

Answer: The foreground emissions were not fully offset by the product-substitution credits.
